rulings.evidence: Sriracha IS a sauce, so the 'sauce' form flag is a wording artefact on the exact vocabulary row Sriracha [sriracha]; a reuse of that declared id. REFUSED the board's hot-sauce bridge - a rooster-bottle sriracha and a generic hot-sauce id are different products and price classes.

limes is a live board id at 5 of 7 stores (cheapest 0.25 at Walmart), so a REUSE and not a proposal - only the vocabulary row is missing, which is a naming question. Same call as the 2026-08-27 'fresh lime juice' -> limes ruling: juice comes from whole limes squeezed, so the purchase basis is 2 whole limes.
The board id is GENERIC lettuce (7 of 7 stores), not a variety-specific id, so this is not the red-onion variety-pricing case; a reuse with the vocabulary row missing. Shredding is a cut, not a food.

rulings.raw: 8 Corn or flour tortillas (store-bought or homemade, warmed)
rulings.evidence: Source offers either; took corn, which has an exact same-form vocabulary row Corn Tortillas [corn-tortillas] and is the standard taco shell. Preferred over the board's generic `tortillas`, which also covers large flour wraps at a different gram weight per piece.
